subject: Private offer: cross-catalog SKU consolidation & channel margin reconciliation
messages:
From: procurement@cloudscale.com (Maria Gutierrez)
To: chloe.martin@redwood.example.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Harmonized pricing for AWS + GCP private offers and channel margin reconciliation

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the latency guarantees. Procurement here at CloudScale received Redwoods private offer proposal for AWS and a separate SKU pack for GCP. We have two asks before we can move to legal:

1) Can Redwood provide a harmonized list-price across the two marketplace catalogs (AWS/GCP) or document acceptable price parity adjustments? Our reseller (NorthBridge) needs consistent list price to calculate commission.

2) We need a clear channel margin reconciliation table showing net-to-Redwood and gross-to-reseller flows (including any escrow or marketplace seller fees).

Attached is the RFP with our billing cadence and compliance checklist. Can you share a proposed approach and timeline?

Best,
Maria Gutierrez
Sourcing Manager, CloudScale
Attachment: CloudScale_RFP_Q3.pdf (pdf, 1 page)
From: chloe.martin@redwood.example.com
To: procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.example.com, irene.choi@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Harmonized pricing for AWS + GCP private offers and channel margin reconciliation

Hi Maria — thanks for the RFP and the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support a harmonized approach and a reconciliation table, and we have two practical paths depending on how you want to consume:

Option A — Catalog parity (recommended for simplicity)
- We publish matched list-price SKUs on AWS and GCP and keep anchor parity within a 3% band.
- Redwood will manage price sync and provide weekly evidence reports for your reseller.

Option B — Regional anchor with settlement (recommended where marketplaces have different fee stacks)
- Maintain marketplace-specific list prices, but Redwood creates a weekly settlement ledger that normalizes to a single commercial price for reseller commission calculations.

For channel margin reconciliation: Jordan and I sketched a sample flow (attached spreadsheet) that breaks down list price -> marketplace fees -> reseller commission -> net retained. It includes an escrow column to hold commissions pending true-up.

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) send the detailed breakdown and assumptions by EOD tomorrow.
2) Quick call Thursday 10:00am PT to confirm which option CloudScale prefers and any NorthBridge constraints.

Attaching the spreadsheet: redwood_crosscatalog_pricing_breakdown.xlsx

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 415 555 0182

On Wed, Jun 11, 2025 at 11:03 AM Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> For channel margin reconciliation: Jordan and I sketched a sample flow (attached spreadsheet) that breaks down list price -> marketplace fees -> reseller commission -> net retained. It includes an escrow column to hold commissions pending true-up.

Maria,

Adding detail on assumptions we used in the spreadsheet so you can validate:
- Marketplace fees: AWS seller fee 6.0% applied at invoice; GCP listing fee 5.2% — we modeled both.
- Reseller commission: NorthBridge asked for a 12% effective rate; we show both fixed-dollar and percentage examples.
- Escrow trigger: if monthly variance between marketplace-reported usage and CloudScale invoice > 7%, commissions are held in escrow and true-up occurs in the following 30-day billing cycle.

Irene is copied for compliance evidence (SOC/retention column in the sheet). Ben, can you confirm whether Redwood Legal is comfortable with a 30-day true-up and escrow holding?

Jordan Blake
Director, Deal Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: redwood_crosscatalog_pricing_breakdown.xlsx

From: ben.carter@redwood.example.com

Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Harmonized pricing for AWS + GCP private offers and channel margin reconciliation

Chloe/Jordan/Irene — quick legal ops note and proposed doc for PO: I've reviewed the proposed escrow true-up cadence. We're OK with 30-day true-up provided the PO includes:
- A defined reconciliation window (30 days) and evidence requirements (marketplace CSV + CloudScale invoice).
- Cap on escrow hold at 20% of monthly reseller commissions to limit cashflow impact.
- Arbitration brief: disputes escalated to Deal Ops within 15 days, then to legal counsel if unresolved.

I've converted the key terms into a PO attachment (PO-Terms-v1.docx) and added a short clause for commission evidence retention (12 months). Chloe — please share the PO doc with Maria and NorthBridge and ask if they want Option A or Option B.

Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: PO-Terms-v1.docx
